articles.title: About the Development Blindspots Lab
articles.subtitle: We measure what official data misses across ADB developing member economies — public sources only, every number from a committed script, every claim under an explicit Constitution.

articles.title: Official registries reorder 16 of 17 Philippine regional facility-load ranks
articles.subtitle: The eight-economy OSM screen is a map-observability triage, not a service-access ranking; only two pilot economies have comparable registry corrections.

articles.title: 90.9 million more people in low-elevation urban centres
articles.subtitle: Named-city GHS-UCDB evidence replaces an inherited national proxy—and narrows the claim from “informal risk” to recorded low-elevation exposure growth, not flood probability or informality.

articles.title: The network is present. Use still lags.
articles.subtitle: Exact-year ITU data show a 14.3-point median difference between reported 4G availability and internet use across 34 ADB developing member cases in 2024.

articles.title: A disaster-recovery ranking fails two validity gates
articles.subtitle: Country burden changes with the metric, while a 108-orbit Haiyan pilot yields no centroid with one recovery month across 54 variants.

articles.title: The top five migrant origins have zero overlap after population normalization
articles.subtitle: Rank emigrant stock by headcount and India and China lead; divide by resident population and Samoa and Tonga take the top — the absolute top five and the share top five share no members, and only Afghanistan is forced-displacement-majority.

articles.title: Flood water cuts modeled market access for about 346,000 people in the Sylhet pilot
articles.subtitle: An observed flood footprint, historical road graph, eight mapped markets, and 54 sensitivity variants replace a national proxy that never measured access — 345,718 modeled people lose every route in the base Sylhet stress test.

articles.title: Only one in nine Nepal rice-price spikes followed locally dry rainfall
articles.subtitle: In 12 Nepali markets over 2020–2025, only 17 of 152 large coarse-rice price jumps followed an unusually dry month. Whatever drove the 2023–24 price wave, local dryness was not the common trigger — and this dataset cannot yet say what was.

articles.title: One urban share can be 20 points from another
articles.subtitle: A GHSL–WDI measurement study across ADB developing economies shows why definition, administrative scale, and reclassification change the urban story.

articles.title: Five economies sit in five or more measurement-gap clusters — Bangladesh, Afghanistan, India, China, Pakistan
articles.subtitle: Across sixteen program screens, Bangladesh appears in eight top-N sets — more than any other economy. The pattern is set membership, not a composite score, and it concentrates in South and Southeast Asia.

articles.title: Two maps of the same health system disagree — and not at random
articles.subtitle: OpenStreetMap shows 17.1 percent of the Philippines' official clinical-tier facility registry and 11.8 percent of Bangladesh's, and the gap is widest exactly where planners need maps most. Any workflow that mixes the two sources needs a reconciliation step first.

articles.title: Population-weighted indices conceal Pacific vulnerability — the per-capita reanalysis
articles.subtitle: When flood and coastal screens are recomputed per million people, the top-5 flips from large South Asian economies to Pacific small-island states. Same data, different scaling, different operational question.

articles.title: A station dot is not yet a coverage claim
articles.subtitle: Across 24 economies, public monitor routes are visible—but not one station completes the chain needed for a verified population-coverage claim.

articles.title: Public station visibility does not validate monitoring coverage
articles.subtitle: The 24-economy public-source audit reaches station discovery and denominator geometry, then stops at identity and monitor-grade evidence—so publish the observability gap, not a coverage estimate.

articles.title: Public monitor routes are visible. Verified coverage evidence is not.
articles.subtitle: Across 24 economies, 239 official station rows and 44 identity candidates yield 0 allowed population-coverage claims.

articles.title: A station on the map is not proof of a working monitor
articles.subtitle: Public dashboards across 24 Asian economies show where air-quality stations sit. No public record confirms, for even one station, that the dot is a currently calibrated regulator-grade monitor — so coverage claims have to wait.

articles.title: Trade volume did not predict observed port delay
articles.subtitle: After testing the inherited imports × logistics-score screen against World Bank vessel-time data, only Indonesia remains in both top fives — and the strongest association points the wrong way.

articles.title: A data year has two clocks
articles.subtitle: In a frozen 18-indicator WDI panel, 19.5% of observed cells change review status when calendar age is separated from indicator-wide production cadence—but environment carries the cross-domain boundary.

articles.title: How to read the program register
articles.subtitle: Four maturity labels tell you what a program may claim — and what it still may not. Read the label with the attestation chain, not as a quality ranking.

articles.title: Five economies where remittance dependence and transfer costs stack up
articles.subtitle: Kyrgyz Republic, Samoa, Tonga, Nepal, and Vanuatu top the joint stress screen — and four of them stay on top under every perturbation tried. Nepal's seat depends on a single threshold choice.

articles.title: Cambodia led the school-heat proxy—but ranked last by observed heatwave disruption
articles.subtitle: The “first in every perturbation” claim is false; among six ADB economies where heatwave was the major 2024 disruption hazard, the proxy’s rank correlation with affected-student counts is +0.03, compared with +0.94 for child population alone.

articles.title: A plausible heat-reliability story fails its regional measurement test
articles.subtitle: The generation-mix result survives a better denominator; the heat-outage direction changes with the proxy.

articles.title: The “stable top five” was fixed by a missing-data rule
articles.subtitle: Two omitted economies outrank the published tail, every named economy had a documented COVID-19 cash-transfer response, and no comparable delivery outcome is joined.

articles.title: "Vol. I, № 04: The first issue of the Blindspots Lab"
articles.subtitle: "Seven programs finished for the current issue, eight at Screening Result, one at Program Prospectus, one at Prepared Pipeline, and one at Hypothesis. Every gate is AI-attested under Constitution §18 — read each headline with that label."

articles.title: The “stable top four” does not survive its own water and crop measures
articles.subtitle: The published set is the raw top four in only two of seven runs; direct water stress retains two members, direct crop concentration none, and the most crop-concentrated visible economies lack water observations.

articles.title: The PM2.5 employment proxy does not recover the heat-work-loss signal
articles.subtitle: Across 21 aligned year-and-parameter tests, the proxy shares at most one of its top three economies with the Lancet Countdown measure of heat-related potential work hours lost.

articles.title: The facility map changes the Philippine regional rank
articles.subtitle: Official clinical registries reorder almost every Philippine regional facility-load rank built from OSM points, so the eight-economy map is a source-validation queue, not a service-access ranking.

articles.title: The PM2.5 proxy does not recover the heat-work-loss signal
articles.subtitle: Across 34 economies and 21 aligned tests, the pollution-and-employment proxy never recovers the heat-related work-hours-loss top three, so it is retired as a heat-loss substitute.

articles.title: Low-elevation urban growth is concentrated in named centres
articles.subtitle: Named urban centres concentrate most of the low-elevation population gain across the reporting GHS-UCDB subset, so city-level joins beat an imputed national proxy for deeper coastal analysis.

articles.title: Network availability is not internet use
articles.subtitle: Reported mobile broadband coverage routinely exceeds internet use in exact-year ADB developing member cases, so coverage alone is not an adoption measure for connectivity monitoring.

articles.title: When a disaster-recovery ranking fails its measurement test
articles.subtitle: Country burden rankings and a GDIS-centroid night-light pilot fail as recovery indicators once alternative burden metrics and multi-specification recovery-month tests are applied.

articles.title: A Sylhet flood-route stress test disconnects about 346,000 people from mapped markets
articles.subtitle: A mechanical road-cut rule inside an observed flood footprint disconnects a large share of baseline market-route population; the share stays narrow across 54 variants, while closure and destination validation remain open.

articles.title: Local dryness preceded only one in nine corrected Nepal rice-price spikes
articles.subtitle: After correcting the market-price outcome, local dryness is a minority near-term signature of large coarse-rice price increases, so the stable result is a measurement boundary, not a climate-effect estimate.

articles.title: A plausible heat-reliability story fails its regional measurement test
articles.subtitle: Exact-year heat–reliability correlations change direction with the heat measure and reliability outcome, so fuel concentration remains a structural-exposure screen while a regional heat-vulnerability ranking does not.

articles.title: When urbanization depends on the definition
articles.subtitle: Harmonized grid urban shares and national-definition urban shares diverge widely across ADB developing-economy cases, so every urban percentage needs the definition stated before comparison or targeting.

articles.title: The leading migrant origins change when population enters the denominator
articles.subtitle: Absolute diaspora scale, population-normalized stock, and forced displacement answer different questions—so they must be read as separate evidence objects, not collapsed into a single migration rank.

articles.title: Trade volume did not predict observed port delay
articles.subtitle: An inherited imports-and-logistics screen fails against observed container-port time: only one economy remains in the old top five, so the ranking is retired as a port-delay measure while the hinterland gate stays open.

articles.title: Show both clocks on public data
articles.subtitle: Calendar age and indicator-relative lag disagree often enough that one calendar-age badge cannot decide both staleness and source-frontier distance—environment carries most of the boundary.

articles.title: When the public map disagrees with the official registry
articles.subtitle: OpenStreetMap and national clinical-tier registries disagree systematically—especially in rural and low-density units—so project preparation cannot read service supply from the map alone.

articles.title: Five DMCs remain in the repaired remittance corridor-cost set
articles.subtitle: After the RPW parser repair, five economies form the baseline joint remittance-dependence and inbound-cost set, with a four-economy sensitivity core—a triage signal, not a country ranking or household exposure estimate.

articles.title: The school-heat ranking fails its first outcome check
articles.subtitle: The proxy that put Cambodia first does not preserve that order among heatwave-major ADB rows in UNICEF's annex, so the national school-heat ranking is retired as a construct-validation failure.

articles.title: The shock-payment “top five” fails its own ranking rule
articles.subtitle: The named shock-payment-readiness set fails its own value order and the COVID-19 response source has no comparable delivery outcome—so publish a construct-validation failure, not a prioritization list.

articles.title: The water-crop “top four” fails direct measurement
articles.subtitle: The inherited four-country agricultural water-risk set is not a persistent raw top four under its own sensitivity rule, and direct water and crop measures do not reproduce it—so the ranking is retired for targeting.

articles.title: Before ranking access, check whether the map contains the facilities
articles.subtitle: A Philippine registry comparison turns an open-map access screen into a more honest source-validation tool.

articles.title: A stable climate-health proxy can still measure the wrong thing
articles.subtitle: Direct heat-labor data overturn the inherited PM2.5 workday-loss ranking.

articles.title: The coastal story changed when the data became spatial
articles.subtitle: Across 1,334 urban centres, low-elevation population grew by 90.9 million from 2000 to 2020—and only two of the old top five economies remain.

articles.title: A signal can reach you before the Internet does
articles.subtitle: Why connectivity dashboards need separate measures for network availability and actual use.

articles.title: The archive worked. The recovery measure did not.
articles.subtitle: Public night-light access scaled for Typhoon Haiyan, but no recovery definition stabilized across the tested variants.

articles.title: The map found the bug—and the flood-route finding survived
articles.subtitle: In Sylhet, 345,718 modeled people—41.24% of those with a baseline market route—lose that route under a flood road-cut stress test, and the share stays 38.92%–43.45% across 54 variants.

articles.title: A stable country screen was still the wrong food-price story
articles.subtitle: Correcting the Nepal market-price outcome turns a climate narrative into a sharper measurement finding.

articles.title: When a good electricity-risk hypothesis meets the wrong data
articles.subtitle: Fuel concentration holds under a stronger generation test, but public heat and reliability series do not support one regional ranking.

articles.title: The same country can have two very different urban shares
articles.subtitle: Across 40 ADB-economy cases in 2020, a standardized urban measure and national definitions differ by a median 20.0 percentage points.

articles.title: A migration ranking can reverse when the denominator changes
articles.subtitle: The same 2024 migrant-stock data tell different stories about diaspora scale and population-relative stock.

articles.title: A national proxy failed when vessel time entered the test
articles.subtitle: Only Indonesia remains in both the inherited trade-logistics top five and the weaker observed port-time set.

articles.title: When “three years old” tells only half the story
articles.subtitle: A better way to show data freshness without hiding age or missingness.

articles.title: Two maps, two answers — and the gap between them is not random
articles.subtitle: Why OpenStreetMap and the official health-facility registry disagree about the same country, and why the disagreement is systematic in a way planners should care about.

articles.title: Five economies stay in the flow-weighted remittance corridor-cost set
articles.subtitle: Kyrgyz Republic, Nepal, Tonga, Vanuatu, and Samoa sit where remittance dependence meets high observed corridor costs—and four of them hold across the full sensitivity suite.

articles.title: A heat proxy is not a school-disruption result
articles.subtitle: Cambodia led the formula, but the first direct outcome check reverses the story.

articles.subtitle: The published top five changes when the panel's own missing-data rule is applied consistently.

articles.subtitle: Only 17 of 152 corrected Nepal coarse-rice spike cells followed locally dry rainfall—and dry alignment stays a minority in all 81 threshold runs.
